title: Offer a way forward. Let the user choose the words.
intro: An immersive scene can still stop at an empty reply box. Reply Inspiration introduces assistance inside the conversation: generate three possibilities, choose one, and bring it into the composer for another edit before sending.

items.label: EXPLORE POSSIBILITIES

figure.alt: Reply Inspiration presents three suggested responses inside the Talkie conversation

items.title: Show a small set of directions.
body: The choices appear in the context of the current exchange. Loading feedback makes the transition into generated suggestions explicit.

items.label: MAKE THE REPLY YOUR OWN

figure.alt: A selected suggested reply appears in the editable message composer before sending

items.title: Selection fills the composer.
body: Choosing a suggestion does not send it. Its text appears in the input, where the user can edit it and decide when to send.

items.title: Ask for inspiration
items.text: The control introduces the response area immediately, followed by a loading state.

items.title: Choose a direction
items.text: Three generated options make the next step concrete without presenting an overwhelming list.

items.title: Edit before sending
items.text: The selected text remains an editable draft. Sending stays a separate action.

items.title: Recover from interruption
items.text: The designs cover cancellation, retained text, generation failure and trying again.

body: The later message-management designs extend that sense of control through editing, recall and rewind. Confirmation and limit states are part of those flows, so changing a conversation is an explicit decision.
